scope: Fast acknowledgement for admitted replies in ButlerRuntime.process (packages/textbutler/src/runtime.ts): a disclosure-wrapped text ack sent after admission and before agent composition, plus the relaxed post-compose supersession check that tolerates the ack's own history echo.

rounds.design: Fire-and-forget Tapback reaction on the triggering message (disclosure emoji or 👀 fallback), unawaited before reply.compose.
blockers: iMessage admits only the six standard Tapback emoji (heart, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, laugh, emphasize, question) and rejects everything else at dispatch — a 🤖 or 👀 ack could never land on the primary provider.

Outgoing reaction echoes cannot be journaled (iMessage returns null messageId for reactions) and therefore attribute to the owner: they bump lastOwnerAt and latestRevision, which would cancel the very reply being acknowledged and suppress the contact for the whole human cooldown.
An indeterminate reaction dispatch leaves an unresolved upstream run that wedges every subsequent dispatch, invisible to `replies reconcile` because the ack was never journaled.

rounds.design: Redesigned as an awaited disclosure-wrapped text ack (`🤖{ … }`): text works on every provider, the echo attributes to the butler via disclosure wrap and journaled acceptedMessageIds, indeterminate dispatch wedges the run honestly, and the post-compose recheck relaxes to a foreign-new-message-id check for acked runs only.
blockers: Ack submit ran outside the contact's dispatching guard, so cancelContact/pause could abort it mid-dispatch and manufacture an indeterminate where the reply path yields a clean cancelled. Fixed by holding this.dispatching across the ack submit, mirroring the reply send.

The foreign-id exemption used the global sent_messages journal, so an owner manual `replies send` landing mid-compose would be excused too — a double-send the old scalar revision check reliably cancelled. Fixed by exempting only this run's acceptedMessageIds via a local Set.
acceptedNits: Beeper may resolve the accepted pendingMessageId alias to a different final provider id; on divergence the ack echo counts as foreign and the run cancels — fail-safe direction.
For acked runs, contact reactions/edits/deletes mid-compose no longer cancel (they add no message id); owner activity still cancels via lastOwnerAt across all kinds.
Hook vetoes now run after the ack is on the wire — the ack means 'seen', semantically defensible.
The ack consumes one grant action and is 1:1 with admitted inbound events.
rounds.verification: iMessage accepted id round-trips to the history row id (guid); WhatsApp ledger is consistent by construction; journal provenance covers cleared-disclosure contacts.

result: Ship. The text ack lands while composition runs, precedes the reply through the serialized lane, journals provenance like any other send, surfaces dispatch uncertainty as a reconcilable indeterminate instead of an invisible upstream wedge, and preserves supersession cancels for any foreign new message.
